content.text:
I submitted composition 22 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46). It gave the highest measured photocurrent, 26.5 µA, under 455 nm light. With only three merit measurements, I can't say whether it's the best in the library.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent | What the XRD showed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **22** | 0.36 / 0.18 / 0.46 | **26.5 µA** | not measured |
| 60 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | 12.6 µA | mainly monoclinic BiVO4 |
| 77 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 | 4.6 µA | a copper vanadate mixed with BiVO4 |

- **Why the BiVO4 region:** BiVO4 is the known visible-light photoanode in this system, and its bandgap (about 2.4 eV) is below the 2.72 eV photons. I started at composition 60, the sample with the most bismuth relative to vanadium. It had the cleanest BiVO4 pattern and a solid result. The last measurement went to its neighbour, 22, which gave about twice the photocurrent.
- **Tried and worse:** composition 77, a copper vanadate, gave only 4.6 µA.
- **Skipped:**
  - The Bi-rich, low-vanadium samples, because that region is likely CuBi2O4, which normally conducts the wrong way for a photoanode.
  - Composition 26, because its XRD showed extra phases alongside BiVO4.

**Not tested:** because 22 beat 60, the best composition may lie a little further toward vanadium. Composition 6 (Bi 0.33, Cu 0.20, V 0.47) is the untested neighbour in that direction. The model's suggestion for the next point wasn't useful after only one data point, so I chose the points myself.

I used all 3 merit measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD scans.
